query: What stratified sampling and weighting procedures yield nationally representative estimates given gender segregation and urban/rural differences?

response.query: What stratified sampling and weighting procedures yield nationally representative estimates given gender segregation and urban/rural differences?
response.answer: Stratified sampling divides the population into subgroups, then random samples are taken from each. Weighting adjusts sample data to reflect the true population proportions, accounting for gender and urban/rural differences. This ensures nationally representative estimates.

results.title: UNSD — Global Calendar of Statistical Events
results.content: This regional training course brings together statisticians and labour analysts from Asia-Pacific national statistical systems to discuss technical aspects and share experiences in the production and use of statistics on informality with the objectives of:1) Assessing progress in the production of statistics on informal employment and employment in the informal sector in Asia and the Pacific Regionand major hindrances in data production;2) Providing technical information and illustrations of good practices on collecting and tabulating data on informal employment and employment in the informal sector aligned to the latest development in labour market standardsand categories of informal workers as well as related data needed for the preparation of SDG indicators;3) Promoting the collection of data and improvement of statistics on informal employment and employment in the informal sector as an integral part of national labour force statistics; and4) Providing guidance and illustrations of good practices on how to conduct diagnoses of informality and how to contextualize indicators to decide on priorities and inform policy development and monitoring.

results.title: Pesticide-Induced Diseases: Sexual and Reproductive Dysfunction
results.content: Gaps in knowledge and further research needs include prospective cohort studies with adequate sample sizes to elucidate the effects of different classes of pesticides (especially emerging insecticides, herbicides and fungicides) and mixture exposures on ovarian health, the development of effective toxicological models that can approximate or simulate realistic human exposure scenarios, and the translation of toxicological findings into measurable indicators that can be used in human health risk assessment. Considering limited epidemiological, biomonitoring, and pathological data on pesticide exposure in women working in tea plantations/gardens, there is an urgent need for well-designed cohort studies to delineate its consequences on reproductive health, pregnancy outcomes, and adverse effects in offspring. Overall, exposure to pesticides with endocrine-disrupting potential raise a particular concern for male fertility because of the possible occurrence of both effects at low concentrations and additive interactions with other environmental risk factors.
